### Dense Order

:::{.definition data-title="Dense Order"}

In mathematics, a partial order or total order $<$ on a set $X$ is said to be
dense if, for all $x$ and $y$ in $X$ for which $x<y$, there is a $z$ in $X$
such that $x<z<y$.

:::

That is, for any two elements, one less than the other, there is another
element between them.

Some examples of sets with dense order include:
- The rational numbers $\mathbb{Q}$
- The real numbers $\mathbb{R}$
